title: Receiving webhooks with signature checks and idempotency
when: An app receives webhook calls from a payment, code hosting or messaging service and must verify they are genuine, ignore replays and duplicates, and answer fast.
prompt:
Goal: POST /webhooks/<provider> verifies an HMAC over the raw body, rejects stale timestamps, stores each event id once and processes it in the background.
Steps:
1. Read the raw body as a Buffer with a size cap before any JSON parsing; the signature covers those exact bytes.
2. Compute createHmac("sha256", WEBHOOK_SECRET).update(timestamp + "." + raw).digest("hex") per the provider docs and compare with timingSafeEqual after checking lengths; mismatch gives 401.
3. Refuse timestamps older than 5 minutes or in the future.
4. Parse, then INSERT INTO webhook_events(event_id, type, received_at, payload) with event_id UNIQUE; a duplicate gets 200 and no work.
5. Enqueue processing and reply 200 or 204 within a few seconds, since providers resend on slow or 5xx replies.
6. During secret rotation accept either of two secrets, then drop the old one.
Quality bar:
- Unknown event types are stored and acknowledged.
- Processing is idempotent by event id.
- The secret lives in config, never in code or logs.
Pitfalls:
- Verifying JSON.stringify(body) instead of the raw bytes.
- Comparing signatures with ===.
- Slow inline work that makes the provider resend.
Verify:
- [ ] A bad signature gives 401.
- [ ] An old timestamp is refused.
- [ ] The same event twice runs once.
- [ ] Tests sign fixtures with a test secret.
Output: routes/webhooks.mjs, the webhook_events migration, test/webhooks.test.mjs.

examples.input: receber webhook de pagamento e nao processar duas vezes
examples.output: raw body HMAC with timingSafeEqual, 5 min window, UNIQUE event_id, enqueue then 200
